newsitem.title: USA: Cosby son's killing latest in Hollywood tragedies.
newsitem.headline: Cosby son's killing latest in Hollywood tragedies.

text.p: Hollywood, TV and music stars are not immune to the tragedy of losing a child, as comedian Bill Cosby learned on Thursday when his only son Ennis was shot dead beside a southern California freeway.
Paul Newman, Marlon Brando, Mary Tyler Moore, Eric Clapton and Francis Ford Coppola are just some of the celebrities who have suffered one of life's deepest personal tragedies -- the loss of a child.

And now Cosby, familiar to so many TV viewers as the perfect, loving father who seemingly handles every crisis with calm aplomb in his successful "The Cosby Show", must face an assault on his real-life family.

Cosby, who also has four daughters, looked red-eyed when he appeared outside his New York apartment on Thursday. He shook his head when reporters asked him to comment about the death of his son. "He was my hero," was all he could say.
Cosby is the latest in a string of celebrities who have suffered such tragedy.
Marlon Brando, one of the screen's biggest stars, suffered the tragedy of a child's suicide when his daughter Cheyenne hanged herself in 1995 in Tahiti.
The suicide was triggered by her half-brother Christian being sentenced to 10 years in prison for the murder five years earlier of Cheyenne's allegedly abusive boyfriend.

Tragedy hit another Hollywood legend when Paul Newman's only son Scott died in 1978 of a drug and alcohol overdose. The movie star and his first wife, Jacqueline Witt, established a foundation in their son's memory.

Years later, in trying to explain the pressures that led to his son's death, Newman commented: "There are about 180,000 liabilities in having me as a father. The biggest one is that there is always an element of competition between children and their parents."
Mary Tyler Moore, the perky optimist of such popular TV comedies as "The Dick Van Dyke Show" and "The Mary Tyler Moore Show", also lost her only son, from her first marriage.
Richard Meeker, 24, died of a gunshot wound to the head when a shotgun he was playing with on his bed while talking on the phone with his girlfriend went off.
At the time of his death in 1980, Moore was starring in the Oscar-winning move "Ordinary People", about one family's problems after a son dies accidentally and another tries to commit suicide.
Recently, Moore told Larry King on CNN that her son's death was an accident and that the type of ultra-sensitive hair-trigger the gun had has now been taken off the market.

Oscar-winning director Francis Ford Coppola's son Giancarlo, 23, was killed in 1986 in a boating accident in Maryland. Coppola, who directed the "Godfather" trilogy, later sued actor Ryan O'Neal's son Griffin for negligence in the incident.

Rock star Eric Clapton's four-year-old son Connor fell to his death in 1991 from the window of the boy's mother's apartment in a New York skyscraper. His death prompted the guitarist to write the Grammy-winning song "Tears in Heaven", and Clapton said the tragedy helped him kick drug and alcohol addiction.

Carroll O'Connor, TV's Archie Bunker in "All in the Family," lost his son Hugh in 1995 to suicide. The actor's son, who appeared with his father in the police series "In the Heat of the Night", shot himself in the head with a shotgun at the age of 33.
O'Connor went to the police and told them a drug dealer had contributed to his son's addiction and subsequent suicide. The man was later jailed for a year for drug trafficking.
Singer and movie star Dean Martin became a recluse and hardly worked again up to his death in 1995 after his son Dino was killed in a plane crash eight years earlier.
